medhx: Hypercholesterolaemia, Chronic kidney disease, Benign prostatic hyperplasia
notes: PSA 12 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.23. Prostate volume 52 mL. csPCa 0.52.

note_sections.t: Persistent PSA elevation alongside a previously negative biopsy warrants specialist consultation.

A retired postal worker, currently 68 years of age, entered initial evaluation for an incidental PSA rise in late 2022, a value that has since advanced to 12.0 ng/mL following a negative systematic biopsy earlier this year. Moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, characterized by nocturia and a diminished stream, are being managed via tamsulosin, yielding an IPSS score of 15. He shares a home with his spouse, engages in light gardening, and follows a largely sedentary lifestyle punctuated by neighborhood walks, alongside a weekly alcohol intake of approximately ten units. Medical background encompasses well-managed hypercholesterolaemia under simvastatin therapy and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, with cardiology assessments in autumn 2024 confirming stable cardiovascular function. An ex-smoker, he accumulated 36 pack-years before ceasing tobacco use in 2017, and previously opted out of prostate cancer research initiatives. He explicitly denies unexplained bone pain, haematuria, or notable weight loss, noting only a resolved right knee arthroscopy from several years prior.

Normal DRE — texture: smooth and rubbery; mobility: unremarkable; asymmetry: absent. The gland presents as symmetrically enlarged without palpable nodules. General survey shows stable vital signs at 130/77 mmHg and a regular pulse of 72 bpm. Abdominal palpation yields a soft, non-tender field with no detectable masses or organomegaly.

admin: Patient declined research participation previously; respect for AS-related trials.
